messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

The reports list includes many events with revisions, times of receipt etc. We need to filter according to knowledge cutoff: only reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (100). Among those reports, for each event_id we choose the highest visible revision (i.e., highest revision number among those with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff). Then we keep these chosen events if event_time <= target_time (i.e., only events up to target_time). Then we apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock, with receipt events adding quantity, demand events consuming min(stock, quantity) and any unmet quantity counted as lost; stockout is when quantity > stock (i.e., unmet > 0). The total historical_lost through target_time is the sum of unmet quantities for all demand events up to target_time. Also we need stock_at_target: after processing all historical events up through target_time (i.e., after all events with event_time <= target_time) we get a stock level; that is stock_at_target.

Then, after the historical reconstruction, we need to apply future_schedule events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from the reconstructed stock (stock_at_target). The future schedule events have times beyond target_time presumably; they go up to horizon_time (130). We need to compute stock after applying all future events up through horizon_time (I think "stock_at_horizon after the scenario" should be the stock after applying all future events up to horizon_time inclusive). In the future schedule, we also count losses (unmet demand) for this scenario only (future_lost), sum of unmet quantities for demand events (including those that cause stockout). The first_future_stockout_time is the earliest future scenario event time (i.e., from future_schedule) with unmet demand >0 (i.e., that caused a stockout). If none cause unmet demand (i.e., all demands are fully satisfied), then output -1. Note: That first future stockout time is relative to the scenario, not historical. But we might need to track from the first future event that produces a stockout, i.e., unmet >0. The time is the event_time of that future event.

We need to be careful: some events may have quantity zero (i.e., they produce no changes). Also note that the raw reports include revision events that may replace earlier values for same event ID. Only those with highest revision are used; lower revisions (including earlier revisions) that were replaced are ignored. This is per event ID.
